features: Sidebar → compact mode now shows tasks as one-line «By task» groups with counts, and the selected row expands to show project, branch, PR, host and agents.
Sidebar → hovering a task number opens its details card, and clicking it opens the task as a tab in the current workspace.
Sidebar → hovering a workspace's «Project on …» label shows its host, live ports and, for task rows, the task details.
Sidebar → a new «Input required» group lists workspaces whose agent is waiting for you, right after Needs attention.
Sidebar → workspaces whose deletion failed are now marked with a «Delete failed» label.
settings: Workspace options → a new switch turns the «Input required» sidebar group on or off; it is on by default.
fixes: «Take to work» into a paired server's worktree now links the agent's session to the task, so the worktree is tracked and cleaned up properly.

features: Sidebar → workspace options adds «By task» grouping: Needs attention, Pinned, Awaiting release (collapsed), In progress and No task sections.
Sidebar → filter menu adds task-state switches that hide workspaces with no task, in progress, or awaiting release; attention rows always stay visible.
Sidebar task workspaces show the task number and title, plus their session state such as Awaiting release, Closing soon, or why they need attention.
Sidebar → a Needs attention workspace's context menu offers Open, Remove anyway…, Keep and Back to work.
Sidebar → Remove anyway… confirms first, listing the branch's own commits, unsaved editor text and any linked workspaces removed with it.
Sidebar → a counter next to the options button shows how many workspaces need attention and switches to «By task» when clicked.
Sidebar → workspace context menu and the Cmd-J palette add «Open task», which opens the task's card.
Issues → «Take to work» now codes one task in its own new workspace named after the task; selecting several tasks disables it.
Issues → taking a task again reopens its workspace only while its session is open; otherwise it starts a new session in a new workspace.
Orca now removes a closed task's workspace automatically when nothing would be lost, and flags it as needing attention otherwise.
Workspaces whose folder was deleted outside Orca are now cleaned up automatically once the folder stays missing.
A paired desktop shows a notification when a closed task's workspace is removed.
Issues → a task card lists its sessions with state, workspace, agent, start and end times, and why a workspace was removed.
Issues → the task list marks tasks whose session is in progress, awaiting release or closing.
Issues → a session in a task card's Sessions list opens the agent's log, read from the machine that ran it.
Mobile app → workspaces can be grouped «By task» with the task-state filter, an attention counter and long-press attention actions.
Mobile app → taking a task again now reopens its open session instead of always starting a new one.
Sidebar → the current workspace's compact row shows its details and running agents, and the hover details card appears after a short pause.
settings: Settings → Build Web and the mobile app's build-web menu add «Auto-remove finished task workspaces»; with it off, closed tasks' workspaces wait for you.
fixes: Sidebar → moving through compact rows with ↑/↓ keeps the selected row in place instead of letting it jump or slip below the fold.

features: The task menu's «All tasks» now opens a searchable task list inside Orca, filterable by status, kind, author and dates, with 25, 50 or 100 per page.
Opening a test run from the task menu now shows that run in the Testing page's history instead of the console's website.
«Build page» on a redo task now shows the build's log inside Orca instead of opening the console's website.
Tasks now show who started them, and you can filter the task list by author.
Tasks Orca cannot open now say so instead of sending you to the console's website.
The phone view gains a «Tasks» section with the same list and filters, opening builds, live job logs and build logs directly.
Redos image builds in the build-web task menu now have a «Build page» button that opens the build's page in your browser.
The build-web task menu gains an «All tasks» entry at the bottom that opens the console's full task list.
Images now shows each RHEL build's RedOS twin status in the distribution column, and each twin shows which RHEL build it comes from.
Copy links in a task's Build tab and in Images asks whether to copy RHEL, RedOS or both; selecting a RHEL build includes its twin.
After a push from Images, the push log follows RedOS twin creation, each image gets a RedOS chip, and a notification appears if a twin fails.
The phone app gets the same RedOS twin display, link copying and push tracking as the desktop.
fixes: Images no longer offers to push a RedOS twin on its own; it is pushed together with its RHEL build.

features: Monorepo products now build for rhel only, and each redos image is derived from its rhel build when published, shown as a redos twin.
Run rows in Trains show redos twin chips: building, full build, awaiting a decision, not built, or no redos, with the rhel build each twin belongs to.
A redos twin that was built but not published offers «Retry» on its run row, and a failed full twin is retried instead of rebuilt.
«Build» on a redos twin awaiting a decision now sends that decision, and older servers that can't accept it explain why they refuse.
Images and «Add image» build products for rhel only and show the console's note when it replaces the requested distribution.
Redos twins are left out of Build all, Rebuild stale/failed, Publish, Testing work rows, and image counts, latest builds and running or failed tallies.
The distribution filter in the build list and Images now appears only for chat-platform, while the distribution column stays everywhere.
The phone app gets the same redos twin chips, Retry and rhel-only building as the desktop.
fixes: When connected to an older build-web console, monorepo builds and distribution filters keep offering rhel, redos or both as before.
A derived redos twin can now be removed once its rhel build has been removed.
The Issues page in the Android phone app now loads instead of failing on build-web data.

features: The phone app's Issues page now shows build-web tasks, with the full task card and all its tabs, replacing the old Tasks view.
You can take a task to work from the phone's Issues page using a Claude account, handled through your paired desktop.
The phone app now has an Images section where you can list, build, push and settle images and view their history and logs.
fixes: Build logs no longer show Jenkins' hidden console notes as stray text.
The new-tab "+" menu in the tab bar shows the "Claude — account" launch rows again, without duplicating them under unavailable chats.

features: Open in now supports opening SSH workspaces in Cursor and Zed, and managed-server workspaces in VS Code over Remote-SSH.
Command-line agent conversations on a paired server can now be continued in the Chat view.
The sidebar lets you open and follow a Claude agent's subagent views, and Codex subagents now show their task names.
The built-in browser now handles Orca shortcuts, split focus and mouse back/forward buttons while a page is focused.
You can watch an agent browse live in the browser pane and jump to that page from the chat.
The browser can dock DevTools inside the browser pane, with a choice of side, resizing and pop-out.
The browser now has a Chrome-style new tab page with a workspace card, suggested sites, and suggestions in the address bar.
The browser asks before a site uses the local network, camera, microphone or location, or opens another app.
The browser asks for a username and password when a site requires one.
Browser tabs playing sound show a speaker icon and can be muted from the tab.
Hovering or focusing a link in the browser shows its URL in a bubble at the bottom of the page.
The browser offers a history view, removable address bar suggestions, and Escape behaviour that matches Chrome.
The browser has a Chrome-style page context menu and DevTools window shortcuts.
The browser explains why a page failed to load and reloads it when it can.
Each site can keep its own appearance and zoom level, set from the page menu or with Cmd/Ctrl +, - and 0.
A loading line along the browser address bar shows page progress, including after link clicks.
Links open in a browser tab beside the pane they came from, and the new tab gets focus.
SSH Hosts lists saved port forwards that couldn't start, explains why, and lets you remove them.
A managed SSH server can be updated with Update or Update anyway while its terminals keep running.
Recover server is offered for a managed SSH host whose server is blocked by a stale lock.
You can open a plain SSH terminal to a host whose move to its Orca server is blocked.
When a managed server can't download Node.js, Orca offers a one-click mirror for both this computer and the host.
After a managed server update, Orca offers to resume your chats.
A native chat gets a fresh automatic name after /clear, and Regenerate name is available from the tab.
Codex chats list the skills Codex loaded, and typing $ in the composer opens them.
Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Grok and Pi chats now show turns that were made outside the chat.
You can remove, paste, drop or attach images on a queued chat message before it is sent.
Chat image previews can be panned and zoomed like diagrams.
Typing /resume in a chat opens Agent Session History.
Claude chats can be rewound at any length by forking the conversation you keep.
A long paste in a chat is attached as a text file, and an oversized message is flagged before sending.
Chat panes have terminal-style header actions for split and close.
Source Control offers Resolve with AI when a merge, rebase or cherry-pick is paused.
Source Control now shows untracked files together with your other changes.
The Resource Manager lists every terminal process and can stop one after confirming.
Orca can reclaim stale dependencies and build output left across worktrees.
Orca's skills install with one click on every setup screen, also on paired servers and SSH hosts, for 11 more agents.
Sidebar rows and tabs show the status that terminal programs report about themselves.
Claude and Codex accounts can be added on a remote server from a paired desktop.
Closing several tabs at once now asks for confirmation; the close-to-the-left and close-to-the-right actions are removed.
File and line locations in PR comments under Checks open directly in the editor.
Session History shows per-agent reading progress, and search hits name the host they came from.
Files dragged from the explorer open in the editor group you drop them on.
HTML file links open as document previews, and new Markdown files open in the rich editor.
Jira issue creation lets you pick users for a required Reporter and other user fields.
The editor now highlights Zig and Lean source files.
Space rows have their own actions menu.
The sidebar shows where a linked reference came from as an icon.
The status bar shows short labels for Antigravity usage pools.
New command-line options list a workspace's detected ports, set a terminal pane's title, and choose chat or terminal when launching an agent.
Orca is now available in Brazilian Portuguese, and onboarding lets you choose a language.
On the phone, the tab strip shows agent state, earlier chat messages load as you scroll up, and the chat composer supports file attachments.
On the phone, Markdown previews have a Copy path button next to Copy.
settings: Settings → SSH Hosts adds a per-host Reconnect on launch toggle and bulk removal of hosts.
Settings → Remote Orca Servers now shows a single list instead of six sections, with sharing at the top.
Settings → Agents lets you choose whether the default agent opens as a chat or as a command-line terminal.
The agent permission setting adds Auto, applies per-agent defaults, and chats now follow it.
Settings → Native Chat adds a custom font family option.
Browser settings let new tabs use a browser profile chosen per repository or per workspace.
Settings → Accounts can sign in to Antigravity, and saves MiniMax and GLM Coding Plan keys on the selected host.
A downloaded agent runtime can be removed from its row in Settings.
The release build picker in Settings now has a search box.
Quick command lists can now hold more than forty commands.
fixes: Ctrl+Tab now cycles floating workspace tabs when the floating panel has focus.
Sidebar text using the match-terminal appearance now uses the terminal's text colour.
Dragging tabs between tab groups now drops them where the cursor actually is.
Pressing Cmd/Ctrl+W now closes the agent terminal dialog in the dashboard.
The Add project host picker and Connect now explain why an SSH host failed.
SSH identity files that use tokens such as %d now resolve correctly.
Orca no longer crashes with "Object has been destroyed" after a window closes.
Folder watching keeps working after macOS asks for a rescan.
A pinned scroll position in the terminal stays in place when old scrollback is trimmed.
Another client's terminal now opens under its own tab instead of a duplicate one.
Claude and Codex panes waiting on the folder-trust dialog now show as needing attention.
A chat tab returns to the terminal when a shell takes over after the agent exits.
Force Reload shows a message when it can't run, instead of silently doing nothing.
Workspaces on a paired server keep their saved tabs across desktop restarts.
Arrow keys move through the remote folder browser when adding an SSH project.
Automation schedules no longer skip or repeat runs around daylight saving time changes.
Find highlights in the terminal stay visible while you move between matches with Cmd+G.
The resource panel on macOS now shows the same memory figure as Activity Monitor.
The collapsed section header in diffs stays in view.
Dropped files on remote workspaces stay out of git, and failed drops or file opens explain why.
Open in VS Code works even when the code command isn't on your PATH.
The System notification sound option now plays the real macOS default sound.
Editors launched from Orca on Linux AppImage builds now start normally.
Claude, Codex and other agents now resume in the folder they last ran in, with their original settings.
Session History now finds Claude, OpenCode, Codex and Copilot sessions it previously missed.
Native chats explain why Claude refused to start, and agent startup failures are described in plain words.
Failed agent starts are retried before your message is rejected.
Keys typed while an agent pane is still starting are kept as an unsent draft.
Codex on Windows switches agents with Alt+Left/Right, and multiline pastes stay one draft.
Ctrl+Enter now works for Claude Code and OpenCode on Windows.
Option+Forward-Delete on macOS now deletes the next word in the terminal.
The + key zooms in on keyboard layouts where it needs no Shift.
Cmd+C no longer pastes on remapped Latin keyboard layouts.
Korean and other IME input now sends on the Enter that finishes composing.
Mac trackpad flicks scroll smoothly in full-screen terminal programs.
Bengali and other Indic scripts now render correctly in the terminal.
Stray "104;255" text no longer appears on agent prompts after switching tabs.
Closing a split pane now moves focus to the neighbouring pane.
Unfocused terminals and chats in a split are now dimmed like editors.
Restart on a failed terminal opens a plain shell instead of Codex.
Restored SSH terminals now recover after a password sign-in.
A terminal saved on a disconnected network drive no longer freezes the window.
Saved SSH port forwards come back after a restart.
The SSH Hosts list no longer crashes with very large SSH configs and can search every host.
Reconnect & Delete now only deletes the workspace you selected.
Remote terminal reconnects show one calm notice per server with the cause.
Saving a file now refuses to overwrite changes made on disk that you haven't seen.
Saves are no longer cancelled, and Don't Save always keeps discarded text off disk.
Tabs of the same file stay in sync after undo or discard, and non-UTF-8 files ask before converting.
Removing a workspace lists unsaved files first and offers their edits back.
Media previews resume from their last playback position, and Cmd/Ctrl +/- zooms open images.
Paragraphs starting with "Dr." or "A." are no longer turned into numbered lists in the editor.
The create-worktree dialog no longer gets stuck when a preflight stalls.
Git no longer drops unmerged branches that have no net file changes.
Stale merged PRs are hidden once a workspace moves to a different commit.
Bitbucket and GitLab SSH remotes on alternate hosts and ports are now recognised.
Linear issue comments are listed oldest first.
The Jira Tasks Board view stays selected after leaving the page.
Usage readings for Claude Enterprise, Cursor Ultra, Kimi and Codex now show the correct figures.
Claude weekly usage no longer jumps back to an idle session's old value.
Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and long-context requests are now priced correctly.
Dismissing a notification no longer closes an open modal editor.
Workspace cycling in the sidebar resumes after you close the last tab.
Workspace hover cards stay open behind link actions and list the newest linked reviews first.
Full shortcut titles are shown on hover in Settings, and shortcut conflicts are reported.
Chinese, Japanese, Korean and French translations are corrected, and missing translations are filled in.
PR merge and close confirmations and Source Control hints are now translated.
Phone pushes open the agent that sent them, and a server without a window sends them.
Many phone app issues are fixed, including lost terminal output, dictation, scrolling gestures and tab names.
Kimi's first prompt is delivered on Windows, and Kimi's trust menu no longer swallows it.
Codex now asks before running MCP tools that require approval.
Chat spelling suggestions appear on right-click, and dropping several images keeps every image.

features: Images page rows now show each image's push state in the Registry column (pushing, pushed or failed) and refresh as each image finishes.
Dev services whose code changed since they started now show a badge with a tooltip listing changed workspaces, unbuilt packages and files.
A changed dev service's badge offers «Rebuild and Restart» to rebuild and restart just that service.
fixes: The dev services status no longer loses the information about what changed since each service started.
A failed dev services build now shows which targets failed with their last output line, and which services did not respond.

features: Images now shows a Freshness column for a picked product version, telling you which images need a rebuild, which are current, or were never built.
Freshness on the Images page distinguishes «rebuild» when an image's own code changed from «packages» when only its shared packages did, with a spinner while scanning.
The Images toolbar has a «Build N» button that builds several picked images of one product together and follows them as a single card.
«Take to work» now shows a loading toast while it creates a new worktree and starts the session, so you can see progress after the dialog closes.

fixes: The Images badge in the sidebar now reflects new builds within about 15 seconds instead of lagging up to three minutes behind.
Images → Create build now opens a dialog listing the versions to build for, instead of building without showing which versions were included.
Images: a task's build with every image removed now shows the new-build form, so you can detect images again and add them to that run.

features: The new-build form in Issues lists the task's release branch and each newer release its commits reach; unticking one leaves it out of that task's builds permanently.
Changing a task's release in Issues reloads its branches so new builds use the new release's branch, and the branch can also be picked by hand.
Leaving Issues and coming back reopens the task and card tab you were on.
A file or task opened from a link in a chat, terminal or source reference now closes on a two-finger swipe back, returning you to where you clicked.
fixes: Task card → Stand and Version lists now show stands and releases added in build-web since the card opened, and a missing release still shows by name.
Clicking a file reference in a remote worktree now opens the file instead of failing with an error.
The Markdown document listing now shows the documents it could read when one folder is unreadable, instead of failing entirely.

features: File names written as inline code, optionally with line numbers, open at that line with Cmd/Ctrl+click in the rich editor and by clicking in Claude chat.
When a file reference matches several files, a menu at the click lets you pick which one to open.
The Markdown view toggle now offers Source, Rich and Preview modes.
fixes: Markdown files now open in Preview by default.

features: Source file references in a plan tab or Markdown preview, such as a file name with a line number, are links that open the file at that line, offering a list when several files match.
The Take to work dialog has an optional instruction field whose text is added to the new session's first message.
Updating a stand from its row on the Stands page keeps you in the table, with progress, outcome and any error shown in the Monitoring cell.
Issues → List offers saved queries that each open in their own tab, and lets you save, share or delete your own filter sets.
Clicking a notification about a failed train or image build opens the matching train window, task or image history in Orca.
The Images page remembers its product, dist, status and version filters, offers a Reset filters button, and picks versions from chips.
fixes: The Stands page now shows Chat Platform stands, which were previously missing.
A stand's Services tab now marks services with a newer build available, matching the to-update count in the Stands table.

features: Each row of the stands table now has an «up -d» button that starts the stand after confirmation and opens its Services tab to follow progress.
Chat Platform is now a full product across Orca: task filters and picker, Images, image builds, task builds, trains and «Take to work» all support it.
The full-screen task card has «Archive» and «Restore» buttons, and archived tasks show who archived them and when.
The task list in Sidebar → Issues gets an «Archive» quick filter for viewing archived tasks; Orca still opens on live tasks.
The comment box on a task card can send a comment to the assignee in Telegram, moving the task to «Awaiting response».
Task comments are marked «Telegram» when sent there and «from Telegram» when the assignee replies from Telegram.
fixes: Sidebar → Images now lists an image building for several distributions at once once per distribution, so the running count matches the sidebar badge.

features: The build-web bell menu now names Telegram rows as «Telegram reply» and «Telegram link request» instead of showing their raw kind.
IS and SDAP task numbers in terminal output become links that open the build-web card in Issues or the Jira issue on Tasks, showing the task title on hover.
Sidebar → Stands shows red and amber counts of down or unhealthy services and services with newer images on running stands.
The Stands list is now a table with Name, Product and Monitoring columns, and stands can be hidden, which also stops their monitoring.
The «to update» chip and the sidebar's amber count now list each service with its running build and the newer one available.
fixes: Claude Code's agents view with background sessions awaiting input no longer shows a red Blocked dot and Needs permission on the worktree.
Stand monitoring no longer counts builds from another registry as updates, only checks running services, and counts stands sharing one host and directory once.

features: The file icon theme chosen in Settings → Appearance now also applies to Source Control's file and folder rows, including changes, staged files and commit history.
A task's Word documents now open read-only in a tab of its worktree, laid out like Word, with Open in Default App as a fallback.
Any .docx opened from the explorer uses the same Word viewer, including on a paired Orca server; old .doc files and files over 3 MB still open in the browser.
The «Take to work» dialog's Agent line lets you pick which Claude account of the worktree's host starts the session, without changing the host's selected account.
fixes: A task's Word documents no longer open in the browser at the console's address instead of inside Orca.
Tab bar → «Claude — account» on a paired server's workspace now starts Claude with that account instead of System default; older servers hide these items until updated.

features: Settings → Appearance → File Icons lets the Explorer show Material Icon Theme icons for files and folders, with light variants on light backgrounds.
The new-tab menu offers «Claude — account» entries to start Claude under another account on the workspace's host for that session only.
The Mockups tab on a build-web task card is now called Artifacts.
The status chip on a build-web task card, full screen or in the side panel, now opens a picker with every available status.
New build-web notifications such as failed builds, console errors or task comments appear as a desktop banner, or as a toast while Orca is in front.
settings: Settings → Appearance gets a File Icons option to choose between Orca's own icons and the Material Icon Theme in the Explorer.
Settings → Notifications gets «build-web» for desktop banners and «build-web Inside Orca» for in-app toasts, both for build-web notifications.
fixes: The plan spec's link to open a task now works again, opening the task's card by its title instead of a removed full-screen button.

features: The titlebar now shows a build-web notifications bell beside the sidebar toggle, with a red unread count for failed builds, console errors and updates to your tasks.
Opening the titlebar bell marks notifications as read; clicking one opens its task's card, and Clear empties the list for you only.
A new tasks icon in the titlebar counts running stand jobs, image builds and test runs, and lists recently finished ones with their status.
Clicking an entry in the titlebar tasks list opens a console job's live log with Cancel, a build's task card, or a test run's console page.
settings: Settings → Integrations can show or hide the titlebar notifications and tasks icons; by default they follow the Issues setting, and they can be hidden from the context menu.
fixes: A task card opened from the titlebar no longer closes on its own the first time a build-web page loads.
In a narrow sidebar header the app name now shortens with an ellipsis instead of cutting off the controls beside it.

features: Right-clicking the status bar now offers "Usage from", letting you pin the usage meters to this computer or a paired server instead of following the focused workspace.
Right-clicking the status bar now offers "All Claude & Codex Accounts", showing a separate usage chip for every account on the chosen host, active account first.
The Claude and Codex account switchers now follow the same host as the usage meters and show usage for that host's inactive accounts.
An unreachable server's accounts in the status bar keep their last usage numbers, marked as stale.
The status bar's usage limit chips now turn green, yellow or red depending on how much of each limit has been used.
Stats & Usage has a picker to show usage for this computer, a paired server, or this computer and all servers together.
fixes: Stats & Usage now counts Claude sessions stored in a custom Claude config folder, which were previously missing from the totals.

features: The status bar shows each connected Orca server's CPU and memory use, with a red dot when either reaches 90% and grey when unreachable.
Issues page: clicking a task title opens its full card as a tab beside a List tab, and open tabs are restored after restarting.
Issues page: clicking the star column header sorts favorite tasks first, and a second click reverses the order.
Live Claude usage now works even when you have your own Claude status line or start Claude with your own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR folder.
The command line can add a Claude account from an existing signed-in folder and give it a name.
settings: Settings → Accounts → Add Folder saves a Claude account from an already signed-in folder on the host, including on remote servers.
Settings → Accounts lets you rename Claude accounts, and the name replaces the email in Settings, the status-bar switcher and switch notices.

features: Each number on the sidebar's Issues, Images, Trains and Testing items now has its own tooltip explaining what it counts.
A page history button pair with a recent-pages list (⟲ ← →) now sits beside the workspace Back/Forward, letting you return to Orca's pages, task cards and recap reports.
Task numbers in Recaps reports are now links that open the task's card full screen, and task-type cells show as coloured chips.
A task's full-screen card, including over the Testing list, now has Plan and Mockups tabs showing the task's plan and its mockup pages.
fixes: The Sidebar → Issues number now counts only open blockers among the tasks the page shows, no longer including done or won't-fix tasks.
In development builds, a task card opened from a link in Issues or Testing no longer closes immediately on its own.

features: Images: clicking «failed» on an image row offers to settle it with the newest successful build of the same image, without rebuilding anything.
fixes: Issues and Testing: Back now reopens the task card you opened an attachment or agent session from, on the same tab and layout.

features: Source Control → branch menu offers «Update from <base>», which fetches the base branch and merges it in, fast-forwarding when the branch has no commits of its own.
Issues → a task's card lists its attached files and each comment's files, opening Markdown, HTML, pictures, PDFs and text in tabs of the task's worktree.
Editor → the line-number menu offers «Git Blame», showing who last changed each line beside the editor, with commit details on hover and the change on click.
Source Control → in the tree view, folders can collapse or expand all their subfolders, section headers fold all folders, and Alt+click toggles a whole subtree.
Images → any successful build can be picked, and «Copy links» copies each image's registry reference with its build number, warning about ones not pushed yet.

fixes: Issues → «Take to work» into a new worktree on a server now opens that worktree and starts its session instead of saying it could not open it.
The Services tab in the right sidebar now stays selected after resizing the panel instead of switching back to Explorer.

features: A new Services tab in the right panel runs a repository's dev services, letting you start profiles, restart, stop, view consoles, open services, and release slots.
Dev services commands configured in a repository's orca.yaml must be trusted like setup scripts, and are re-checked on every run, including on remote hosts.
Testing now opens on two tabs: «In testing» shows the current watch, and «Test history» lists past runs by day, filterable by All, Nightly or Manual.
Testing → Test history opens a run with its changes since the previous run, a workspace map, a per-test breakdown, each test's last 14 runs, job logs and junit.xml.
The sidebar's Testing item shows, in red, how many tests failed in the newest finished nightly run.
The sidebar's Trains item shows how many images are in windows that are building or deploying right now.
A task opened from Testing now gets a wider dialog, up to 1536 pixels across.
Recaps now opens as a month calendar showing each report on the day it finished; click one to open it, then Escape returns to the calendar.
Recaps has a «Calendar | List» switch, remembers the view you picked, and applies the product, version and automation filters to the calendar too.
A new sidebar item, «Stands», lists the AP, DC and SA stands, with each stand's services, their state, image, tag, build number and build date.
Stands lets you restart one service or bring the whole stand up again, after confirming, and follows the job and its log on the page.
Stands shows a service's log with a choice of how many recent lines to load, live following, and Cmd/Ctrl+F search with highlights.
Stands → Users lists a stand's UI logins, filterable by application; «Log in» opens the stand in Orca's browser and fills in the login form.
Application chips on Stands use the same colours as on Issues: SA purple, DC blue and AP green.
The build log dialog on Images uses the new log viewer, so you can search it with Cmd/Ctrl+F.
In a train window, each image now shows whether it is «pushed», «built, not pushed» or «held», with the reason it was held.
The source editor supports go to definition across files for TypeScript, JavaScript and Python, with Cmd/Ctrl+click, F12 and Peek.
The source editor has Back and Forward buttons and shortcuts for moving between the places you jumped to, including mouse side buttons.
The source editor has an Outline panel beside the code, toggled from the editor header, with a filter, the current symbol highlighted, and click-to-jump.
«Take to work» names the session after its tasks' keys and titles, and taking the same tasks again reopens that session.
settings: The «Work in this worktree» option in the «Take to work» dialog is removed, along with its remembered choice.
fixes: The images in a train window now update as each build finishes, instead of keeping their old state while another image is still building.
Pushing an image now updates the train window, and its tags column no longer lists tags of images that were not pushed.
Images → «Push to registry» now sends every picked build even if one is refused; refused images are named and stay selected.
«Take to work» no longer lets the task skill create its own worktree; Orca creates one only when you choose «Create a new worktree».
When «Take to work» creates a new worktree, its base branch is always chosen from the repository's branches, and the session starts only once one is picked.

releases.note: Everything this custom build adds to Orca
features: The main menu has a new «Changelog» item right after «About Orca», listing each release's new features, settings and fixes, with the installed one marked.
A new «Issues» sidebar page lists build-web tasks with Mine, For AI, Favorites, Jira and To work quick filters, status and product filters, search and stars.
Issues → task list shows coloured chips, sortable columns, pages of 50, an assignee column, and status, priority and assignee changeable straight from the row.
Issues → task list marks tasks handed to AI or held by an agent session, and shows subtasks folded under their task with a subtask count.
The Issues sidebar item counts open top-priority blockers among the tasks matching the page's current filters.
Clicking a task in Issues opens a resizable side card where the title, description, steps, status, priority, assignee, release and «handed to AI» are edited in place.
A task opens full screen with Overview, Build, Guide & Jira, Commits and Subtasks tabs, laid out like build-web's own task card.
Task card → Overview has comments with a composer that can also post to Jira, and your own comments can be corrected or deleted.
Task card → Build adopts or creates a run, shows image freshness and progress, and builds, rebuilds, cancels, removes and publishes images, with build logs in a dialog.
Task card → Guide generates and revises the guide live, takes screenshots from a chosen stand, and publishes it to the task's Jira issue.
Task card → Properties sets assignee, product, stand, release, type, priority and build destination, and subtasks inherit the rest from their parent.
Task card → Subtasks lists each subtask with an in-place status, and warns while open subtasks block moving the task onward.
Card panels and commit lists in the full-screen task card resize by dragging or arrow keys, and their widths are remembered per tab.
«Take to work» sends picked tasks to a new Claude session in an existing or new worktree, named after the task keys.
«Take to work» on a task whose session is still open switches to that session instead of starting a second one.
A new «Images» sidebar page shows each image's newest build with filters, sortable columns, build history and push to the registry.
The Images sidebar item counts images building now and, in a red chip, images whose newest build failed.
Images → build dialog starts a new image build, prefilled from the last build, with a «Run tests» option that is off by default.
Images shows each push's progress in a card with per-image results and its log, then refreshes the table when the push finishes.
Images has «in progress» and «failed» filters by last build status, and build logs open in a dialog that follows the newest lines.
A new «Trains» sidebar page lists build-web's build trains with their windows, a «What boards now» preview and a «Depart now» button.
Trains → a history row opens its window in a «Run» dialog with status, images, tasks, errors, publications and the journal on request.
A new «Testing» sidebar page lists tasks in testing whose images are not yet out, with «Check now» and chips showing the work left.
Testing → the work-left chips open the push or build menu directly, and a task opens in a dialog over the list.
A new «Recaps» sidebar page lists finished build-web automation reports, newest first, filterable by product, version, automation and date range.
Recaps → the selected report shows beside the list in a resizable panel, with its charts and diagrams, following Orca's theme.
A new «Git» page shows every branch's commit log with a graph, branch tree, changed files and diffs, plus branch and commit operations.
Custom builds now update from build-web's «Orca» feed instead of GitHub, and an offered update links to build-web's release page.
An app window that is older than its loaded code now asks you to restart instead of showing a cryptic error.
settings: Settings → Notifications has a new «Only When an Agent Needs Input» switch, off by default, limiting alerts and the Dock badge to agents waiting on you.
Settings → Integrations has a Build Web card to connect, test, replace or disconnect build-web and to bring back hidden Issues, Images, Trains, Testing or Recaps items.
fixes: A remote server no longer fails to start its Orca daemon after its third daemon update.
Custom builds can again deploy to servers over SSH and are no longer treated as older than the newest official release.
The Trains sidebar item now appears for people already connected to build-web, following the Issues item until set on its own.
The Issues sidebar item now opens the task list instead of the card left open, and the card's breadcrumb returns to the list.
The Images sidebar count now refreshes within a minute, and immediately on build-web pages or after starting a build.
Long lines in a commit diff now wrap inside their own column instead of running over the other side.
Resizable column splits in task card tabs no longer stop dragging immediately after you start.
